mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above the 5-year moving average coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its 5-period SMA by at least 25 bps in a single month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward returns remain positive despite persistent FEDFUNDS above SMA, or the 5-period SMA does not retrace within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in unemployment claims followed by a sustained decline in the unemployment rate predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investor sentiment deteriorates on labor market weakness.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a single month and UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points in the following month
regime_hint: Early signs of a labor market softening
failure_condition: Over 12 months, the 60-day forward returns remain positive whenever the trigger occurs, or unemployment recovers without a sustained negative sentiment shock.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive month of rising home sales (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) above their 12-month averages precede a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals resilient consumer and business demand.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and INDPRO both exceed their respective 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns remain negative despite repeated triggers, or the pattern persists for >6 months without a positive return episode.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals supply-side constraints and muted demand.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >2% in a single month and CPIAUCSL decreases by >0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is positive whenever the trigger occurs, or the pattern reverses within 2 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below the 10-year low, the S&P 500 exhibits a positive 20-day forward return as expectations of future easing lower discount rates and boost equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below its 10-year minimum
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns remain negative even after multiple consecutive easing signals, or the 10-year low is not established.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in job openings (not directly observable in the provided proxies) but proxyable by a combination of PAYEMS and UNRATE dynamics—specifically, a sharp drop in UNRATE after a large monthly increase in PAYEMS—predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return due to increased labor market uncertainty.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >15% in a month and UNRATE falls by >0.3 percentage points in the following month
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are consistently positive during such triggers, or the UNRATE decline is not followed by a sustained downward sentiment.

mechanism_narrative: A two consecutive months of declining retail sales proxies (none available in this catalog; instead, use HOUST as a proxy for consumer demand) and rising industrial production (INDPRO) predict a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals demand softening without sufficient supply response.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases for two consecutive months while INDPRO increases in the same months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive whenever the trigger occurs, or the pattern reverses within 10 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the UNRATE (labor market slack) for three consecutive months in a non-recessionary regime is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it reflects expectations of future wage growth and reduced policy tightening risks.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls for three consecutive months and remains below 4.5% for the next month
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns remain negative even after UNRATE declines persist, or the regime is identified as recessionary.
